brief: BofA's weekly catalyst note argues that this week's August inflation data decides the September FOMC hike. Its economists forecast core CPI up 0.22% m/m and core PCE up 0.24% m/m, which would put core PCE at a 2.9% annualized pace and 3.4% year over year, above the 2% target, and in their view enough to convince Chair Warsh that higher rates are warranted. They continue to expect 75bp of hikes this year, after what the note calls a hawkish payroll print. Because hike risk brings credit concerns forward, the strategists prefer Large Cap Value as ballast: across credit stress cycles since the 90s the second half of the spread widening ran six times faster than the first and always came with negative S&P 500 returns. Favored value industries are oil and gas, distributors, metals and mining, banks and leisure products. Media and IT Services are flagged as value traps. Separately, Bessent's higher 10y+ buyback cap makes this week's long-end operation a test: a take-down short of the max would temper expectations and cheapen long-end rates further. Tal Liani likes Oracle's risk/reward into the 10 September 1Q27 print, price objective $240.
